LESSON: SQUARES AND SQUARE ROOTS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Numbers
Topic 1.4: Squares and Square roots

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Squares and Square roots
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What is the difference between regular and irregular shapes?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify common plane figures (square, rectangle, triangle, circle)
2. tell the difference between regular and irregular shapes
3. find the perimeter of a rectangle by adding all sides
4. find the perimeter of a square by adding all sides (or 4 × side)
5. use cm and m correctly when measuring length

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ What is a plane figure?

• A plane figure is a flat shape.
• It has length and width, but not thickness you can hold like a box.
• Common plane figures: square, rectangle, triangle, circle.

▸ Regular and irregular shapes

• Regular shapes have a clear, definite figure (square, rectangle, equilateral triangle, circle).
• Irregular shapes do not look the same on all sides / do not follow one simple equal-side rule.
• Kenyan look-around examples of rectangles: exercise book, door, window, TV screen, table top.
• Kenyan look-around examples of squares: some stools, tiles, window panes, pillows.

▸ Units of length (revision)

Teach
• We measure length in centimetres (cm) and metres (m).
• 1 m = 100 cm.
• To change m → cm: multiply by 100.
• To change cm → m: divide by 100.

Worked example
• 9 m to cm → 9 × 100 = 900 cm.
• 590 cm to m → 590 ÷ 100 = 5 m 90 cm.

Try this
• Convert 3 m to cm.
• Convert 250 cm to m and cm.
• (Check later: 3 m = 300 cm; 250 cm = 2 m 50 cm)

▸ What is perimeter?

Teach
• Perimeter = the distance all the way round a closed shape.
• Start at one point, go round every side, return to the start.
• For any polygon: add the lengths of all sides.

Worked example
• A triangular flower bed has sides 3 m, 4 m, and 5 m.
• Perimeter = 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 m.

Try this
• Sides 2 m, 6 m, 7 m. Find the perimeter.
• (Check later: 15 m)

▸ Perimeter of a rectangle

Teach
• A rectangle has 4 sides.
• Opposite sides are equal: two lengths (L) and two widths (W).
• Perimeter = L + W + L + W.
• Or: Perimeter = 2 × (L + W).

Worked example
• Exercise book: L = 18 cm, W = 13 cm.
• P = 18 + 13 + 18 + 13.
• 18 + 13 = 31, then 31 + 18 = 49, then 49 + 13 = 62.
• Perimeter = 62 cm.
• Check with formula: 2 × (18 + 13) = 2 × 31 = 62 cm.

Try this
• Door: L = 200 cm, W = 100 cm. Find the perimeter.
• Classroom board: L = 240 cm, W = 120 cm. Find the perimeter.
• (Check later: Door P = 600 cm; board P = 720 cm)

▸ Perimeter of a square

Teach
• A square has 4 equal sides.
• Perimeter = side + side + side + side.
• Or: Perimeter = 4 × side.

Worked example
• A square tile has side 15 cm.
• P = 4 × 15 = 60 cm.

Try this
• Square handkerchief side 25 cm. Find P.
• Square garden side 8 m. Find P.
• (Check later: 100 cm; 32 m)

▸ Irregular shapes

• Measure (or read) every side.
• Add all sides carefully.
• Keep the same unit (all cm, or all m).

Worked example — irregular 5-sided plot
• Sides: 4 m, 3 m, 5 m, 2 m, 6 m.
• P = 4 + 3 + 5 + 2 + 6 = 20 m.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• Rectangle book: 18 cm × 13 cm → P = 62 cm.
• Door: 200 cm × 100 cm → P = 600 cm.
• Square tile side 15 cm → P = 60 cm.
• 9 m = 900 cm; 590 cm = 5 m 90 cm.

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Find P of a rectangle 16 cm by 9 cm. Show both addition and 2(L+W).
2. Find P of a square of side 12 cm.
3. Convert 7 m to cm, then find P of a square of side 7 m in cm.
4. An irregular shape has sides 10 cm, 8 cm, 6 cm, 8 cm, 10 cm. Find P.
5. Word problem: A rectangular classroom is 9 m by 6 m. What length of skirting board is needed to go all round?

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Measure a book, a phone, or a desk top with a ruler. Record L and W. Calculate perimeter.
2. Draw 1 rectangle, 1 square, and 1 irregular shape. Label sides. Find each perimeter.
3. Write 5 perimeter questions for a friend. Then mark them.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is the difference between regular and irregular shapes?
2. How do we find perimeter?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Perimeter = distance round a closed shape.
• Rectangle: P = 2(L + W).
• Square: P = 4 × side.
• Always use the same units (cm or m).

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
